- [ ] **Step 4: Rewrite the catalog panel**

Replace the whole of `src/ui/catalog-panel.ts` with:

```ts
import type { CatalogGroup } from '../catalog/navigation';
import type { CatalogComponent } from '../catalog/schema';
import { CATALOG_GLOSSARY } from './catalog-glossary';
import { button, element } from './dom';

/**
 * The catalog panel (PHASE2-TODO items 6 and 7, MI-UX-020, ADR 0012 and
 * ADR 0014): every entry, grouped by period in catalog order, each a button
 * that zooms to its component and selects it. Groups are native disclosures;
 * a group's buttons are built the first time it opens, so the 4,016-entry
 * core costs nothing until then. Periods 5 to 12 arrive after the first
 * stable frame (addGroups); until then the panel lists the curated periods
 * and says that the rest is loading.
 */
export type CatalogCoreState = 'loading' | 'ready' | 'failed';

export interface CatalogPanel {
  readonly element: HTMLElement;
  /**
   * Marks the selected entry (aria-current) and opens its group; undefined
   * clears the mark. A selection the panel did not make itself (a marker, a
   * link) also scrolls its entry into view inside its list, without moving
   * focus or the page.
   */
  setSelected(id: string | undefined): void;
  /** Adds the groups of periods not listed yet; the groups already shown, and focus, stay. */
  addGroups(groups: readonly CatalogGroup[]): void;
  /** The line below the groups that says whether periods 5 to 12 have arrived. */
  setCoreState(state: CatalogCoreState): void;
}

const HINT_ID = 'catalog-panel-hint';

const countText = (count: number): string =>
  `${count.toLocaleString('en-US')} component${count === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;

const CORE_STATE_TEXT: Readonly<Record<CatalogCoreState, string>> = {
  loading: 'Loading periods 5 to 12…',
  ready: '',
  failed: 'Periods 5 to 12 could not be loaded. Reload the page to try again.',
};

function createGlossary(): HTMLElement {
  const glossary = element('details', { className: 'catalog-glossary' });
  const terms = element('dl');
  for (const { term, definition } of CATALOG_GLOSSARY) {
    terms.append(element('dt', { text: term }), element('dd', { text: definition }));
  }
  glossary.append(element('summary', { text: 'About periods, rays and addresses' }), terms);
  return glossary;
}

/** Scrolls `list` so that `item` is inside it, centred if it was outside; nothing else moves. */
function revealWithin(list: HTMLElement, item: HTMLElement): void {
  const top = item.offsetTop;
  const bottom = top + item.offsetHeight;
  if (top >= list.scrollTop && bottom <= list.scrollTop + list.clientHeight) return;
  list.scrollTop = Math.max(0, top - (list.clientHeight - item.offsetHeight) / 2);
}

export function createCatalogPanel(options: {
  readonly groups: readonly CatalogGroup[];
  readonly onActivate: (component: CatalogComponent) => void;
}): CatalogPanel {
  const root = element('section', {
    className: 'catalog-panel',
    attributes: {
      'aria-labelledby': 'catalog-panel-heading',
      'data-catalog-core': 'loading',
    },
  });
  const entries = new Map<string, HTMLButtonElement>();
  const openers = new Map<string, () => void>();
  const periods = new Set<number>();
  let selectedId: string | undefined;
  /** Set while one of the panel's own buttons activates an entry, so it is not scrolled away. */
  let activatingId: string | undefined;

  const createEntry = (component: CatalogComponent): HTMLLIElement => {
    const entry = button(component.label, { className: 'catalog-entry' });
    entry.dataset['catalogId'] = component.id;
    entry.setAttribute('aria-describedby', HINT_ID);
    if (component.id === selectedId) entry.setAttribute('aria-current', 'true');
    entry.addEventListener('click', () => {
      activatingId = component.id;
      try {
        options.onActivate(component);
      } finally {
        activatingId = undefined;
      }
    });
    entries.set(component.id, entry);
    const item = element('li');
    item.append(entry);
    return item;
  };

  const createGroup = (group: CatalogGroup): HTMLDetailsElement => {
    const details = element('details', { className: 'catalog-group' });
    details.dataset['period'] = String(group.period);
    const summary = element('summary', { className: 'catalog-group__summary' });
    summary.append(
      element('span', { text: `Period ${group.period}` }),
      // Keeps the period and the count apart in the accessible name.
      element('span', { className: 'visually-hidden', text: ', ' }),
      element('span', {
        className: 'catalog-group__count',
        text: countText(group.components.length),
      }),
    );
    const list = element('ul', { className: 'catalog-group__list' });
    details.append(summary, list);
    let built = false;
    const open = (): void => {
      if (!built) {
        built = true;
        list.append(...group.components.map(createEntry));
      }
      details.open = true;
    };
    details.addEventListener('toggle', () => {
      if (details.open) open();
    });
    for (const component of group.components) openers.set(component.id, open);
    if (group.openByDefault) open();
    return details;
  };

  const coreStatus = element('p', {
    className: 'catalog-panel__status',
    text: CORE_STATE_TEXT.loading,
  });
  const groupsBox = element('div', { className: 'catalog-panel__groups' });

  const addGroups = (groups: readonly CatalogGroup[]): void => {
    for (const group of groups) {
      if (periods.has(group.period)) continue;
      periods.add(group.period);
      const next = [...groupsBox.children].find(
        (child) => Number((child as HTMLElement).dataset['period']) > group.period,
      );
      groupsBox.insertBefore(createGroup(group), next ?? null);
    }
  };

  root.append(
    element('h2', {
      className: 'eyebrow',
      text: 'Catalog',
      attributes: { id: 'catalog-panel-heading' },
    }),
    element('p', {
      className: 'catalog-panel__hint',
      text: 'Choose a component to zoom to it and inspect it.',
      attributes: { id: HINT_ID },
    }),
    groupsBox,
    // Where periods 5 to 12 will appear, so that nothing above moves when they do.
    coreStatus,
    createGlossary(),
  );
  addGroups(options.groups);

  return {
    element: root,
    setSelected: (id) => {
      if (id === selectedId) return;
      if (selectedId !== undefined) entries.get(selectedId)?.removeAttribute('aria-current');
      selectedId = id;
      if (id === undefined) return;
      openers.get(id)?.();
      const entry = entries.get(id);
      entry?.setAttribute('aria-current', 'true');
      const list = entry?.closest<HTMLElement>('.catalog-group__list');
      if (id !== activatingId && entry !== undefined && list !== null && list !== undefined) {
        revealWithin(list, entry);
      }
    },
    addGroups,
    setCoreState: (state) => {
      root.dataset['catalogCore'] = state;
      coreStatus.textContent = CORE_STATE_TEXT[state];
      coreStatus.hidden = state === 'ready';
    },
  };
}
```

```bash
  let catalogIndex = createCatalogIndex(COMPONENT_CATALOG);

  function namesOf(
    components: readonly CatalogComponent[],
  ): ReadonlyMap<string, CatalogComponent> {
    return new Map(
      components.flatMap((component) =>
        [component.id, ...component.aliases].map((name) => [name, component] as const),
      ),
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the matcher**

Create `src/catalog/find.ts`:

```ts
import type { CatalogComponent } from './schema';

/**
 * The catalog panel's find field (owner decision 2026-10-17, ADR 0014). A
 * query is one of three forms, tried in this order:
 *
 * 1. One or two ray fractions, such as `3/7` or `6/15 and 9/15` (separated
 *    by spaces, a comma or "and"): an entry matches when it has a
 *    characteristic ray equal to each fraction, by value, so `2/5` also finds
 *    the rays 6/15. The main cardioid's rays are 0/1 and 1/1.
 * 2. Text starting with `mi-`: a prefix of the entry's id or of an alias, so
 *    `mi-p4-02` finds its v1 alias and `mi-p12-` lists period 12.
 * 3. Anything else: the label contains the text, ignoring case and treating
 *    every run of punctuation and spaces as one space ("period 2" finds the
 *    "Period-2 bulb"); the match starts at a word start and, when the text
 *    ends in a digit, also ends at a word end, so `period 1` does not find
 *    period 12.
 *
 * Matches come back in the order given (the catalog order), at most `limit`.
 */

export const FIND_RESULT_LIMIT = 50;

export interface FindResult {
  /** The first `limit` matches, in input order. */
  readonly matches: readonly CatalogComponent[];
  /** How many entries match in all. */
  readonly total: number;
}

type Matcher = (component: CatalogComponent) => boolean;

const FRACTIONS = /^(\d{1,5})\/(\d{1,5})(?:(?:\s*,\s*|\s+and\s+|\s+)(\d{1,5})\/(\d{1,5}))?$/;

const raysOf = (component: CatalogComponent): readonly [number, number][] =>
  component.characteristicRays?.map(
    (ray) => [ray.numerator, ray.denominator] as [number, number],
  ) ?? [
    [0, 1],
    [1, 1],
  ];

const fractionMatcher = (fractions: readonly [number, number][]): Matcher | undefined => {
  if (fractions.some(([, denominator]) => denominator === 0)) return undefined;
  return (component) =>
    fractions.every(([numerator, denominator]) =>
      raysOf(component).some(([n, d]) => n * denominator === numerator * d),
    );
};

const escapeRegExp = (text: string): string => text.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

/** Lower case, with every run of characters other than letters, digits and "/" one space. */
const words = (text: string): string =>
  text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}/]+/gu, ' ')
    .trim();

const labelMatcher = (text: string): Matcher | undefined => {
  const phrase = words(text);
  if (phrase === '') return undefined;
  const end = /\d$/.test(phrase) ? '(?![0-9])' : '';
  const pattern = new RegExp(`(?:^| )${escapeRegExp(phrase)}${end}`, 'u');
  return (component) => pattern.test(words(component.label));
};

/** The matcher for a query, or undefined when the query is empty or cannot match. */
export const catalogMatcher = (query: string): Matcher | undefined => {
  const text = query.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').toLowerCase();
  if (text === '') return undefined;
  const fractions = FRACTIONS.exec(text);
  if (fractions !== null) {
    const values = [fractions.slice(1, 3), fractions.slice(3, 5)]
      .filter(([numerator]) => numerator !== undefined)
      .map(
        ([numerator, denominator]) => [Number(numerator), Number(denominator)] as [number, number],
      );
    return fractionMatcher(values) ?? (() => false);
  }
  if (text.startsWith('mi-')) {
    return (component) =>
      [component.id, ...component.aliases].some((name) => name.startsWith(text));
  }
  return labelMatcher(text) ?? (() => false);
};

/** Every entry matching `query`, the first `limit` of them listed; undefined for an empty query. */
export const findInCatalog = (
  components: readonly CatalogComponent[],
  query: string,
  limit = FIND_RESULT_LIMIT,
): FindResult | undefined => {
  const matcher = catalogMatcher(query);
  if (matcher === undefined) return undefined;
  const matches: CatalogComponent[] = [];
  let total = 0;
  for (const component of components) {
    if (!matcher(component)) continue;
    total += 1;
    if (matches.length < limit) matches.push(component);
  }
  return { matches, total };
};
```

Replace the whole of `src/ui/catalog-panel.ts` with:

```ts
import { findInCatalog, type FindResult } from '../catalog/find';
import type { CatalogGroup } from '../catalog/navigation';
import type { CatalogComponent } from '../catalog/schema';
import { CATALOG_GLOSSARY } from './catalog-glossary';
import { button, element } from './dom';

/**
 * The catalog panel (PHASE2-TODO items 6 and 7, MI-UX-020, ADR 0012 and
 * ADR 0014): a find field, then every entry grouped by period in catalog
 * order, each a button that zooms to its component and selects it. Groups are
 * native disclosures; a group's buttons are built the first time it opens, so
 * the 4,016-entry core costs nothing until then. The core arrives after the
 * first stable frame (addGroups); until then the panel lists the curated
 * periods and says that the rest is loading.
 */
export type CatalogCoreState = 'loading' | 'ready' | 'failed';

export interface CatalogPanel {
  readonly element: HTMLElement;
  /**
   * Marks the selected entry (aria-current) and opens its group; undefined
   * clears the mark. A selection the panel did not make itself (a marker, a
   * link) also scrolls its entry into view inside its list, without moving
   * focus or the page.
   */
  setSelected(id: string | undefined): void;
  /** Adds the groups of periods not listed yet; the groups already shown, and focus, stay. */
  addGroups(groups: readonly CatalogGroup[]): void;
  /** The line below the groups that says whether periods 5 to 12 have arrived. */
  setCoreState(state: CatalogCoreState): void;
  /**
   * Shows "Zoomed to <label>." beside the list after a list activation, on
   * layouts where the canvas is above the panel (styles.css). It is not a
   * live region: the canvas toast already announces the zoom.
   */
  confirm(component: CatalogComponent): void;
}

const DESCRIPTION_ID = 'catalog-panel-hint';
const FIND_ID = 'catalog-find';
const FIND_HINT_ID = 'catalog-find-hint';
/** Quiet time before the match count is written (and announced) while typing. */
const COUNT_DELAY_MS = 400;

const countText = (count: number): string =>
  `${count.toLocaleString('en-US')} component${count === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;

const resultText = (result: FindResult, loading: boolean): string => {
  const suffix = loading ? ' Periods 5 to 12 are still loading.' : '';
  if (result.total === 0) return `No component matches.${suffix}`;
  if (result.matches.length < result.total) {
    return `${countText(result.total)} match; showing the first ${result.matches.length}.${suffix}`;
  }
  return `${countText(result.total)} ${result.total === 1 ? 'matches' : 'match'}.${suffix}`;
};

const CORE_STATE_TEXT: Readonly<Record<CatalogCoreState, string>> = {
  loading: 'Loading periods 5 to 12…',
  ready: '',
  failed: 'Periods 5 to 12 could not be loaded. Reload the page to try again.',
};

function createGlossary(): HTMLElement {
  const glossary = element('details', { className: 'catalog-glossary' });
  const terms = element('dl');
  for (const { term, definition } of CATALOG_GLOSSARY) {
    terms.append(element('dt', { text: term }), element('dd', { text: definition }));
  }
  glossary.append(element('summary', { text: 'About periods, rays and addresses' }), terms);
  return glossary;
}

/** Scrolls `list` so that `item` is inside it, centred if it was outside; nothing else moves. */
function revealWithin(list: HTMLElement, item: HTMLElement): void {
  const top = item.offsetTop;
  const bottom = top + item.offsetHeight;
  if (top >= list.scrollTop && bottom <= list.scrollTop + list.clientHeight) return;
  list.scrollTop = Math.max(0, top - (list.clientHeight - item.offsetHeight) / 2);
}

export function createCatalogPanel(options: {
  readonly groups: readonly CatalogGroup[];
  readonly onActivate: (component: CatalogComponent) => void;
  /** Brings the canvas into view (the confirmation's button); focus stays put. */
  readonly onShowView: () => void;
}): CatalogPanel {
  const root = element('section', {
    className: 'catalog-panel',
    attributes: {
      'aria-labelledby': 'catalog-panel-heading',
      'aria-describedby': DESCRIPTION_ID,
      'data-catalog-core': 'loading',
    },
  });
  /** Group entries and find results by catalog id; either may be absent. */
  const entries = new Map<string, HTMLButtonElement>();
  const results = new Map<string, HTMLButtonElement>();
  const openers = new Map<string, () => void>();
  const searchable: CatalogComponent[] = [];
  const periods = new Set<number>();
  let selectedId: string | undefined;
  /** Set while the panel's own button activates an entry, so it is not scrolled away. */
  let activatingId: string | undefined;
  let confirmedId: string | undefined;
  let coreState: CatalogCoreState = 'loading';
  let countTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;

  const createEntry = (
    component: CatalogComponent,
    registry: Map<string, HTMLButtonElement>,
  ): HTMLLIElement => {
    const entry = button(component.label, { className: 'catalog-entry' });
    entry.dataset['catalogId'] = component.id;
    if (component.id === selectedId) entry.setAttribute('aria-current', 'true');
    entry.addEventListener('click', () => {
      activatingId = component.id;
      try {
        options.onActivate(component);
      } finally {
        activatingId = undefined;
      }
    });
    registry.set(component.id, entry);
    const item = element('li');
    item.append(entry);
    return item;
  };

  const groupsBox = element('div', { className: 'catalog-panel__groups' });

  const createGroup = (group: CatalogGroup): HTMLDetailsElement => {
    const details = element('details', { className: 'catalog-group' });
    details.dataset['period'] = String(group.period);
    const summary = element('summary', { className: 'catalog-group__summary' });
    summary.append(
      element('span', { text: `Period ${group.period}` }),
      // Keeps the period and the count apart in the accessible name.
      element('span', { className: 'visually-hidden', text: ', ' }),
      element('span', {
        className: 'catalog-group__count',
        text: countText(group.components.length),
      }),
    );
    const list = element('ul', { className: 'catalog-group__list' });
    details.append(summary, list);
    let built = false;
    const open = (): void => {
      if (!built) {
        built = true;
        list.append(...group.components.map((component) => createEntry(component, entries)));
      }
      details.open = true;
    };
    details.addEventListener('toggle', () => {
      if (details.open) open();
    });
    for (const component of group.components) openers.set(component.id, open);
    if (group.openByDefault) open();
    return details;
  };

  const findInput = element('input', {
    className: 'catalog-find__input',
    attributes: {
      id: FIND_ID,
      type: 'search',
      autocomplete: 'off',
      spellcheck: 'false',
      'aria-describedby': FIND_HINT_ID,
      'aria-controls': 'catalog-find-results',
    },
  });
  const findCount = element('p', {
    className: 'catalog-find__count',
    attributes: { role: 'status', 'aria-live': 'polite', 'aria-atomic': 'true' },
  });
  const resultList = element('ul', {
    className: 'catalog-find__results',
    attributes: { id: 'catalog-find-results', 'aria-label': 'Matching components' },
  });
  resultList.hidden = true;
  const coreStatus = element('p', {
    className: 'catalog-panel__status',
    text: CORE_STATE_TEXT.loading,
  });
  const confirmationText = element('span', { className: 'catalog-panel__confirmation-text' });
  const showView = button('Show the view', { className: 'catalog-panel__show-view' });
  showView.addEventListener('click', () => {
    options.onShowView();
  });
  const confirmation = element('p', { className: 'catalog-panel__confirmation' });
  confirmation.append(confirmationText, showView);
  confirmation.hidden = true;

  const runFind = (): void => {
    const result = findInCatalog(searchable, findInput.value);
    if (countTimer !== undefined) clearTimeout(countTimer);
    results.clear();
    if (result === undefined) {
      resultList.replaceChildren();
      resultList.hidden = true;
      groupsBox.hidden = false;
      findCount.textContent = '';
      return;
    }
    resultList.replaceChildren(
      ...result.matches.map((component) => createEntry(component, results)),
    );
    resultList.hidden = false;
    groupsBox.hidden = true;
    countTimer = setTimeout(() => {
      findCount.textContent = resultText(result, coreState === 'loading');
    }, COUNT_DELAY_MS);
  };
  findInput.addEventListener('input', runFind);
  findInput.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (event.key !== 'Escape' || findInput.value === '') return;
    // Escape clears the field first; the document's Escape (legend isolation) waits.
    event.preventDefault();
    findInput.value = '';
    runFind();
  });

  const findField = element('div', { className: 'catalog-find' });
  findField.append(
    element('label', {
      className: 'catalog-find__label',
      text: 'Find a component',
      attributes: { for: FIND_ID },
    }),
    findInput,
    element('p', {
      className: 'catalog-find__hint',
      text: 'By name, id or rays, such as rabbit, mi-p4-6-9 or 6/15.',
      attributes: { id: FIND_HINT_ID },
    }),
    findCount,
  );

  const addGroups = (groups: readonly CatalogGroup[]): void => {
    for (const group of groups) {
      if (periods.has(group.period)) continue;
      periods.add(group.period);
      searchable.push(...group.components);
      const details = createGroup(group);
      const next = [...groupsBox.children].find(
        (child) => Number((child as HTMLElement).dataset['period']) > group.period,
      );
      groupsBox.insertBefore(details, next ?? null);
    }
    if (findInput.value.trim() !== '') runFind();
  };

  root.append(
    element('h2', {
      className: 'eyebrow',
      text: 'Catalog',
      attributes: { id: 'catalog-panel-heading' },
    }),
    element('p', {
      className: 'catalog-panel__hint',
      text: 'Choose a component to zoom to it and inspect it.',
      attributes: { id: DESCRIPTION_ID },
    }),
    findField,
    resultList,
    groupsBox,
    // Where periods 5 to 12 will appear, so that nothing above moves when they do.
    coreStatus,
    confirmation,
    createGlossary(),
  );
  addGroups(options.groups);

  const mark = (id: string, current: boolean): void => {
    for (const registry of [entries, results]) {
      const entry = registry.get(id);
      if (current) entry?.setAttribute('aria-current', 'true');
      else entry?.removeAttribute('aria-current');
    }
  };

  return {
    element: root,
    setSelected: (id) => {
      if (id !== confirmedId) {
        confirmation.hidden = true;
        confirmedId = undefined;
      }
      if (id === selectedId) return;
      if (selectedId !== undefined) mark(selectedId, false);
      selectedId = id;
      if (id === undefined) return;
      openers.get(id)?.();
      mark(id, true);
      const entry = entries.get(id);
      const list = entry?.closest<HTMLElement>('.catalog-group__list');
      if (id !== activatingId && entry !== undefined && list !== null && list !== undefined) {
        revealWithin(list, entry);
      }
    },
    addGroups,
    setCoreState: (state) => {
      coreState = state;
      root.dataset['catalogCore'] = state;
      coreStatus.textContent = CORE_STATE_TEXT[state];
      coreStatus.hidden = state === 'ready';
      if (findInput.value.trim() !== '') runFind();
    },
    confirm: (component) => {
      confirmedId = component.id;
      confirmationText.textContent = `Zoomed to ${component.label}.`;
      confirmation.hidden = false;
    },
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write ADR 0014**

Create `docs/decisions/0014-generated-catalog-core.md`:

```markdown
# ADR 0014: The generated period ≤12 catalog core

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-10-17
- Amends: [ADR 0004](0004-catalog-disposition.md) (workstream F ships as a
  product feature), [ADR 0011](0011-catalog-schema-v2-and-stable-ids.md) (the
  generation method, the period-4 labels, the encoded form),
  [ADR 0012](0012-catalog-navigation-and-marker-density.md) (the find field,
  one panel description, the asynchronous hand-over, the label width)
- Trace: [PHASE2-TODO item 7](../verification/PHASE2-TODO.md#7-generated-period-12-catalog-workstream-f-as-a-product-feature);
  owner decisions Q3, Q4 and "Item 7 (2026-10-17)"; `MI-PERF-003`,
  `MI-PERF-008`, `MI-VER-PERF-003`, `MI-UX-020`

## Context

The owner chose (Q3) to ship the full period ≤12 core, 4,016 hyperbolic
component centres, generated with a pinned arbitrary-precision tool and
independently cross-checked, with generated labels and curated names where
known. Item 6 built the list, the marker density policy and the viewport
index and tested them on a synthetic catalog of that size. The generator
could not reach period 5: its Durand–Kerner root finder does not converge on
the degree-16 polynomial. ADR 0011 sized an encoded form at about 137 KiB
against a 256 KiB budget. On 2026-10-17 the owner added a find field, labels by
rays for every generated entry, and an in-panel confirmation on narrow layouts.

## Decision

**Root isolation.** For each Lavaurs ray pair of exact period p, both
parameter rays are traced in binary64 (`landing_center`) and must land within
1e-9 of each other. Newton's method in 80-digit `decimal` arithmetic refines
the landing point. Complex ball arithmetic, with every rounding bounded by the
operands' magnitudes, then encloses g(c) = f_c^p(0) at the refined point and
g' over the disk of radius 1e-50 about it, and the Krawczyk test proves that
the disk holds exactly one root of g, a simple one (`tools/catalog_certify.py`).
The same enclosure of f_c^d(0) excludes 0 for every proper divisor d, so the
period is exact. The disks of one period are disjoint, so the 4,016 pairs name
4,016 distinct centres. Since the roots of g are simple and the number of
centres of exact period p is the A000740 count, they are all of them. Only the
Python standard library is used. The stored centre is the nearest binary64.

**The ray pair of each centre is proved** (owner decision 2026-10-17), in the
cross-check (`tools/crosscheck_rays.py`). For every c in the proved disk about
a record's centre, the dynamic rays of f_c with the record's angles a/M and b/M
land at one point:

1. Far out the Böttcher map is close to the identity: for |z| ≥ 2 and |c| ≤ 2,
   φ_c(z) = z·e^δ with |δ| ≤ η = (|c|/|z|²)/(1 − |c|/|z|²). Disks about the
   straight rays therefore enclose every ray of the two doubling cycles for
   |w| in [20, 400], one fundamental domain of potential.
2. Pulling a chain of disks back by ±√(w − c) encloses the next fundamental
   domain of the ray of half the angle. At each disk the sign is the one whose
   image meets the disk already known at the junction; if both or neither
   meet, the proof stops.
3. Once one period of potential of both rays lies in a disk D on which every
   w ∈ D has exactly one solution of f^p(z) = w in D (the Krawczyk test with
   the target ranging over D), the inverse branch maps D into a compact part
   of itself. Its iterates carry each ray's later pieces into D and shrink
   them to its unique fixed point, so both rays land there.

Ball arithmetic in binary64, with every rounding bounded, proves 4,014 pairs
within 744 pull-backs. The period-12 component nearest −2, whose landing
point lies 1.4e-13 from c, needs 40-digit decimals about a disk of radius below
1e-24 that the cross-check proves about its centre (96 pull-backs). The pairs
themselves must be Lavaurs' pairs, which the cross-check recomputes.

The rest is mathematics. By the wake theorem (Douady and Hubbard; Milnor 2000,
"Periodic orbits, external rays and the Mandelbrot set", Theorem 1.2 and its
corollaries), the dynamic rays of a characteristic pair land together exactly
for c in the closed wake of that pair, so each centre lies in its pair's wake.
Every other period-p component in a wake lies in the wake of a smaller
period-p pair. The centres are proved distinct and complete, so by induction
from the innermost pairs, each centre is the one at whose root its pair's
parameter rays land. Not computed, and imported from the literature: the
landing of periodic parameter rays in Lavaurs' pairs (Douady and Hubbard;
Lavaurs 1986), the wake theorem, the nesting of wakes, and the simplicity of
the roots of f_c^p(0) (Gleason). The binary64 path assumes only IEEE-754 binary64
conformance with round-to-nearest: it uses +, −, ×, ÷ and the square root,
which IEEE-754 rounds correctly, and exact operations (the absolute value of a
real, `frexp`, `ldexp`). Magnitudes are sqrt(x² + y²) and complex square roots
the real formulas, with each rounding inside the allowance of 8 × 4.5e-16
relative per operation, and the rays' directions come from decimal Taylor
series with a bounded remainder; no C-library function (`hypot`, `cmath`,
`exp`, `sin`, `cos`) enters a bound. Beyond that, the proofs trust Python's own
exact integers and correctly rounded `decimal` arithmetic.

**Independent cross-check.** `tools/crosscheck_catalog_core.py` reads only the
shipped files and imports none of the generator's modules. It recomputes the
counts by the Möbius formula and compares them with A000740, and evaluates
f_c^p(0) and its derivative exactly in integer arithmetic at each stored
binary64 centre. Rouché's theorem then proves that a disk of four Newton steps
about it holds exactly one simple root (the generator uses the Krawczyk test
at the 80-digit point), with f_c^d(0) bounded away from 0 for every proper
divisor. It also checks the residuals to three digits, every exact-period
angle used once, both rays sharing a kneading sequence, exact conjugate
closure, the half-plane invariant, real centres exactly where the rays are
symmetric and in angle order along the axis, disjoint disks, and a finite,
positive `componentSizeEstimate` for every entry.

| Measured on the planning laptop (2026-10-17)             | Value                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Generation (`catalog:core:check`), one core              | 95–102 s (Lavaurs pairing 13 s, ray tracing most) |
| Cross-check with the ray proofs, 4 or 8 processes        | about 3 minutes (7.4 minutes in one process)      |
| Components per period                                    | 1, 1, 3, 6, 15, 27, 63, 120, 252, 495, 1023, 2010 |
| Largest distance from a stored centre to its proved root | 1.12e-16                                          |
| Largest \|f_c^p(0)\| at a stored centre (period 12)      | 1.33e-10                                          |
| Smallest proper-divisor \|f_c^d(0)\| at a stored centre  | 0.00154                                           |
| Closest centres of one period (period 12)                | 7.06e-6 apart                                     |
| `catalog/core.v1.bin`                                    | 136,560 bytes (133.4 KiB; 88.7 kB compressed)     |

**Encoding.** `catalog/core.v1.bin` is a 16-byte header (magic `MICORE`,
format version 1, maximum period, record size, count) and 4,016 records of 34
bytes, little-endian, in catalog order: the period (u8), the lower and upper
ray numerators over 2^p − 1 (u16 each), the centre as two binary64 values
(exact round trip), `centerPrecisionDigits` (u8), and the three residuals as
float32 of their three-significant-digit values. One method and one
provenance apply to every record, so the manifest `catalog/core.v1.json`
holds them, with the counts per period, the length, the SHA-256 and the
SHA-256 of each generator source. Ids, labels and both addresses are derived
on load; the angled addresses by Schleicher's closed-form rules
(`src/catalog/combinatorics.ts`), which agree with the generator's tuned
sub-wake method on all 4,015 entries of period 2 to 12. The curated JSON
stays as it is: it is reviewed text, and the five names, the aliases and the
annotations come from it.

**Checks.** Regeneration takes about 100 s and the cross-check about three
minutes, so `npm run check` runs only `catalog:core:inputs` (0.15 s): the
generator sources must hash to the manifest's `inputs` and the binary to its
SHA-256, so a generator change without a regeneration fails at once. The
`Catalog core` workflow (`.github/workflows/catalog-core.yml`) regenerates the
core byte for byte and runs the cross-check on pull requests that change
`catalog/`, the generator or cross-check tools or their tests, on every push
to main, and on request (owner decision 2026-10-17);
`npm run catalog:core:verify` runs the same locally.

**Loader off the main thread.** After the first stable frame, a worker fetches
the binary, checks its length and SHA-256 against the manifest, decodes it to
validate every record, and transfers the bytes back. The main thread decodes
them again, without the addresses, which are computed when first read: 8.5 ms
in Chromium and 20 ms in Firefox, then 7 ms and 16 ms to merge the curated
entries, build the index and add the panel's groups. A structured clone of the
decoded objects instead cost 63 ms of main-thread time in Chromium.

**While the core loads**, the panel lists periods 1 to 4 and says "Loading
periods 5 to 12…" where the new groups will appear, so nothing above them
moves; the markers are the curated ones. If the file is unreachable or does
not match its manifest, the panel says that periods 5 to 12 could not be
loaded, and the curated catalog and rendering are unaffected (MI-PERF-003).

**Links before the core.** A link's `sel=` with a v1 alias or a period ≤4 id
resolves at once, as before. A well-formed id of period 5 to 12 (two rays of
exact period with one kneading sequence) is kept, stays in the address bar,
and is selected when the core arrives; if the core has no such entry, the link
notice says that the selected component was not found. `v` stays 1.

**Labels.** Every generated entry is labelled
`Period <p>, rays <a>/<2^p−1> and <b>/<2^p−1>`, the six period-4 entries
included; only the five named
components keep curated names. Ids do not change. A marker whose label starts
with its period is named `Inspect <label>`, without a repeated period.

**Find field.** Above the groups, a search field filters by one or two ray
fractions (by value, so `2/5` finds 6/15), by an `mi-` prefix of an id or
alias, or by label text from a word start (a trailing number must end a word,
so `period 1` does not find period 12). Results replace the groups while a
query is active: at most 50 buttons in catalog order, with a polite count
("2,010 components match; showing the first 50.") written 400 ms after typing
pauses. Each result is a normal Tab stop (no roving tabindex); Escape clears
the field. The search reads the data, not the DOM, so unbuilt groups need not
open.

**Lazy groups at scale.** A group builds its buttons once, on first open or
when a selection inside it arrives; a selection from a marker or a link
scrolls its entry into view inside the group's 20rem list without moving focus
or the page. Building the 2,010 period-12 buttons takes 34–39 ms in Chromium
and 47–55 ms in Firefox on a quiet machine (121 ms under heavy load); the
owner accepted the Firefox figure, at the long-task threshold, as measured
(2026-10-17).

**Narrow layouts.** At 68rem and narrower, where the panel sits below the
canvas, a list activation shows "Zoomed to <label>." with a Show the view
button, sticky at the bottom of the panel; focus stays on the entry. It is not
a live region: the canvas toast already announces the zoom once.

**Screen readers.** The panel region carries the one description ("Choose a
component to zoom to it and inspect it."); entries no longer each point to it.

**Marker density on real geometry (Q4).** The policy is unchanged, as the owner
confirmed (2026-10-17). Placed
markers: 29 at the default view on a 922×576 canvas and 16 on 300×225; 25 and
15 at the rabbit (8×); 27 and 11 at the 13× corpus view; 5 at 126×.
Collisions, not the cap, bound the count. Walking further periods would reach
40 on the desktop default view only, with twice the entries examined, while
the phone canvas saturates at 18 even when all 4,016 are examined; so the walk
still stops at the first period that brings the candidates to 40.

**Label width.** Generated labels are 9.5rem (period 4) to 13.7rem (period 12) wide in both engines, so the marker label maximum is 14rem (it was
11rem), and the policy's label box estimate caps at the same width.

## Alternatives rejected

- **Evidence for the ray pairs** (both rays traced in binary64 to the same
  root, plus invariants): rejected by the owner, who asked for a proof.
- **Proving the parameter rays' landing instead**: they land at parabolic
  roots, where convergence is slow and the Krawczyk test degenerates; the
  dynamic rays at a centre land at a repelling point.
- **Durand–Kerner or Aberth on the full polynomial**: degree 2,048 at
  period 12, O(d²) per sweep in Python decimals, with no proof of isolation.
- **mpmath or another arbitrary-precision library**: a new pip dependency; the
  standard library's `decimal` and integers suffice.
- **A JSON or text core**: shortest round-trip decimals and three residuals
  cost about 87 bytes per entry (about 350 kB), over the budget.
- **Regenerating the core in `npm run check`**: it would double the check
  (52 s) for a file that changes only with its generator, which the input
  hashes already catch.
- **Posting decoded objects from the worker**: 63 ms of structured-clone
  time on the main thread.
- **`content-visibility: auto` on long lists**: it halves the period-12 build
  (15–18 ms in Chromium) but skipped entries take a placeholder height, so the
  scroll into view lands outside the list.
- **Live-region confirmation**: it would announce the zoom twice.

## Consequences

- The catalog grows from 11 to 4,016 entries; the main bundle grows by
  12.8 kB (28.4 kB compressed), and a 5.5 kB worker and the 136.6 kB core
  load after the first frame.
- The six period-4 labels change: "Period-4 component 2" is now "Period 4,
  rays 6/15 and 9/15". Their ids and v1 aliases are unchanged.
- At the default desktop view the core adds 18 markers of periods 5 and 6;
  the advisory `catalog-overlay.png` and `selected-marker.png` baselines
  change, and the owner regenerates them in the container. The colourised
  goldens do not change: markers are DOM outside the buffer.
- Regenerating the core needs about 100 s; `catalog/README.md` says how.
```

````markdown
# Component catalog

The Mandelbrot Interiority catalog lists every hyperbolic-component centre of
exact period one through twelve: 4,016 entries. It has two files of data and
one of curation.

## Files

- `components.v2.json` holds the eleven entries of period one to four in
  schema v2 ([ADR 0011](../docs/decisions/0011-catalog-schema-v2-and-stable-ids.md)).
  The application imports it at startup. It is generated; never edit it by
  hand. Regenerate it with
  `python3 tools/generate_catalog.py --write catalog/components.v2.json`.
- `core.v1.bin` and its manifest `core.v1.json` hold all 4,016 entries
  through period twelve in a compact binary form
  ([ADR 0014](../docs/decisions/0014-generated-catalog-core.md)). The
  application loads them in a worker after the first frame. They are
  generated; regenerate both with
  `python3 tools/generate_catalog_core.py --write catalog` (about 100 s).
- `curation.v2.json` holds what a person reviewed: the names of the five
  named components, the v1 ids each entry keeps as aliases, and optional
  annotations, keyed by canonical id. Every other entry is labelled by its
  rays, for example "Period 4, rays 6/15 and 9/15". Edit it, then regenerate
  `components.v2.json`; the core does not store labels.

## Ids

An entry's id is `mi-p<p>-<a>-<b>`: its period and the numerators of its two
characteristic rays over `2^p − 1` (the main cardioid is `mi-p1-0-1`). The id
depends only on the component, so regeneration never changes it. The v1 ids
(`mi-p1-main`, `mi-p3-rabbit`, `mi-p4-01`…) are aliases that resolve forever,
because share links (ADR 0009) name them in `sel=`. Never remove an alias.

## What each entry records

- `center`: the nearest binary64 to the centre refined by Newton's method in
  80-digit decimal arithmetic, proved by the Krawczyk test to lie within
  1e-50 of exactly one simple root of exact period, and
  `centerPrecisionDigits`, its correct significant digits (at most 16).
- `period`, `internalAddress`, `angledInternalAddress` and
  `characteristicRays`, all generated from the rays (the main cardioid has no
  angled steps and no ray pair). The core stores only the period and the rays;
  the loader derives the rest.
- `residual`: |f_c^p(0)|, the distance to the refined centre, and the
  smallest |f_c^d(0)| over proper divisors d, at the stored centre.
- `annotation` (optional, curated): one line of at most 280 characters, shown
  in the inspector under the entry's name (ADR 0012).
- `method` and `provenance`: keys into the `methods` and `provenance` tables
  (in `components.v2.json`, and in the core's manifest), which say how the
  fields were computed and which were curated.

## Validation

```sh
npm run catalog:test            # the generator, certification and cross-check unit tests (Python)
npm run catalog:check           # regenerates components.v2.json and requires byte equality
npm run catalog:core:inputs     # the core's manifest matches its sources and its bytes (fast)
npm run catalog:core:verify     # regenerates the core byte for byte, then cross-checks it
```

`npm run check` runs the first three. `catalog:core:verify` takes about five
minutes (three of them the cross-check, in parallel processes); the
`Catalog core` workflow runs it when the catalog or its tools change and on
every push to main. The cross-check (`tools/crosscheck_catalog_core.py` and
`tools/crosscheck_rays.py`) shares no code with the generator. It proves each
stored centre's root again in exact integer arithmetic, checks the counts
against OEIS A000740, the residuals, divisor periods and conjugate closure,
recomputes Lavaurs' ray pairs, and proves that each pair's two dynamic rays
land together at its centre; with the wake theorem this proves which pair
belongs to which centre (ADR 0014). The unit tests in `tests/unit/catalog/`
check the loaded files, and the loaders (`src/catalog/schema.ts`,
`src/catalog/core.ts`) reject a malformed file.

The catalog data is dedicated to the public domain under
[CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). The generator
and application source remain licensed under GPL-3.0-only.

## Phase 2 role

The catalog is a navigation, testing and explanation feature, not a
performance dependency ([ADR 0004](../docs/decisions/0004-catalog-disposition.md)):
the renderer never reads it. The curated layer stays intact; the core extends
it, and the explorer falls back to the curated layer when the core cannot be
loaded.
````

Run this script from the repository root. Each replacement asserts that its text occurs once (table edits are confined to the named row), so a mismatch stops it:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path


def replace_once(path: str, old: str, new: str) -> None:
    file = Path(path)
    text = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if text.count(old) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: expected the text once, found {text.count(old)}:\n{old}")
    file.write_text(text.replace(old, new), encoding="utf-8")


def replace_in_row(path: str, row_start: str, edits: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
    """Edits one Markdown table row, found by how it starts."""
    file = Path(path)
    lines = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(keepends=True)
    rows = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line.startswith(row_start)]
    if len(rows) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: expected one row starting {row_start!r}, found {len(rows)}")
    row = lines[rows[0]]
    for old, new in edits:
        if row.count(old) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"{path}: row {row_start!r}: expected {old!r} once")
        row = row.replace(old, new)
    lines[rows[0]] = row
    file.write_text("".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")


def append(path: str, text: str) -> None:
    file = Path(path)
    file.write_text(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip("\n") + "\n" + text, encoding="utf-8")
```

## Notes for the owner

1. **The association proof imports theorems.** The computation proves, for every centre, that its pair's two dynamic rays land together (and that the pairs are Lavaurs'). The step to "this centre is that pair's" uses published results: the wake theorem (a characteristic pair's dynamic rays land together exactly for parameters in its closed wake; Milnor 2000, Theorem 1.2 and its corollaries), the landing of periodic parameter rays in Lavaurs' pairs (Douady–Hubbard; Lavaurs 1986), the nesting of wakes, and Gleason's simple roots. ADR 0014 lists them. The binary64 path assumes only IEEE-754 binary64 conformance with round-to-nearest: magnitudes, complex square roots and the rays' directions are built from correctly rounded operations, and no C-library function enters a bound; the decimal fallback and the exact checks trust Python's own integer and `decimal` arithmetic.
